summary: Establish ground-truth for evaluation
description:
## Story

As an OLS developer, I want to establish ground-truth answers, so that we can evaluate OLS response quality.

Currently we are using ground-truth answer to evaluate the response. It is essential to ground-truth answers are correct.

Approach:

* First evaluate that answers are correct/relevant for each query for any QnA pair.
* Then check that answers are grounded against given context.
* Tune system prompt for above steps.
* Use multiple models to check both 1st and 2nd steps.
* Select best QnA pairs.

[Reference](https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/facts-grounding-a-new-benchmark-for-evaluating-the-factuality-of-large-language-models/)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Write a script which will select best possible QnA pairs (do steps mentioned in above approach.

summary: Truncate tool responses to keep tokens within context window
description:
## Description:

As a OLS developer I want to limit the token usage for tool calling, so that we don't exceed context window. 

## Acceptance Criteria

* Propose the algo/logic on how the truncation happens to avoid the tool calls filling up context window.  
  Possible solutions .
* Reserve tokens for tool output (some percentage of context window)
* Truncate the initial tool output when above limit is reached.
* total available tokens for prompt + context + history is context_window - response_token - reserved tool token

  

Note:

If we don't reserve tokens for tool, then it is possible that history will utilize maximum available tokens. And during tool calling we may get error due to context_window limit. Without this change user has to terminate current session and start conversation

summary: [UI] No error message when secret doesn't exist
description:
When the OLSConfig references a Secret that doesn't exist, there is no specific error message to explain that the Secret is missing, just a generic error message. Since this is probably a common situation, it would be good UX to provide a more helpful error message.

We should at least have a pointer to the fact that the secret doesn't exist or that something is preventing the creation of the service pod and therefore the associated errors.

Issue: Generic error message is displayed

Expected: Error message stating that the setup isn't complete, that the secret is missing or pointing the user to check the OLSConfig resource since the status will state the secret is missing.

summary: Send intermediate tool call model response to the user
description:
## Description:

As a OLS user, I want to see the commands that is executed by OLS so that I can see how the answer is formed.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Send tool choice from model to user in natural language form. 
* Send output of the tool calls to user in natural language form. 
* Send the final answer 
* Create a UI story if the console cannot handle the streamed intermediate output

### Note

* We can utilize current streaming mechanism to send intermediate tool call details to the user. The actual LLM call can happen with/without streaming, so we need a compatible response object which will work in both scenarios. 

* With tool call, we don't get any text from the LLM. So we need to humanize the text for user. Example: Calling <Function Name> with <ARG1_NAME>=<ARG1_VALUE>...

summary: [tests] Adapt tests to not have to delete namespace everytime
description:
Every time we call the tests for a new provider, we run a [cleanup of the namespace](https://github.com/openshift/lightspeed-service/blob/main/tests/scripts/utils.sh#L51). This is unnecessary and costs some time to reinstall the operator. Since we're working with the same operator version everytime we run the tests, we can simply change the OLSConfig and restart the controller deployment and wait for the service to be ready yet again.

We should see improvements in the time it takes to run the tests.

 

## Acceptance criteria:

* Adapt clean up to update the OLSConfig and restart the controller deployment (this can be done during the tests and remove the existing clean up)

summary: F-02 LLM Question Validation Bypass (Prompt Injection)
description:
During the pentest it was found that it is possible to bypass validation and force the assistant to answer questions outside of the OpenShift context.  
It was also found that it is possible to receive instructions that were given to the assistant.

At the moment it can lead to usage of the assistant not in the intended way. However, once the assistant gets permissions to query information from the cluster, it can lead to severe security issues.

Details and PoC can be found in the PenTest report that will be distributed to team members.

summary: F-03 Service Account with Excessive Permissions
description:
The service account 'lightspeed-operator-controller-manager' is bound to a ClusterRole with excessive permissions that allow clusterwide access to sensitive resources secrets, cluster roles, cluster role bindings, among others.

In the event that any of the service account tokens are compromised by any means, a privilege escalation path exists to take over the entire cluster. 

Details and Poc can be found in the PenTest report that will be distributed to team members.

summary: Add network policies for kube resources
description:
## Description

As a OLS developer I want OLS kube resources to have network policies, so that attackers cannot make unrestricted communication.

## Acceptance Criteria

\*add network policies for kube resources

Threat: Without network policies, any pod within the Openshift cluster can communicate freely with other pods, regardless of their intended level of access. Attackers or compromised pods can exploit this lack of restriction to move laterally within the cluster and potentially compromise critical components. In the absence of network policies, pods may have unrestricted communication with external networks, this can result in unintended data leakage, where sensitive information is transmitted to unauthorized destinations.

summary: h11 accepts some malformed Chunked-Encoding bodies
description:
### Impact

A leniency in h11's parsing of line terminators in chunked-coding message bodies can lead to request smuggling vulnerabilities under certain conditions.

### Details

HTTP/1.1 Chunked-Encoding bodies are formatted as a sequence of "chunks", each of which consists of:

* chunk length
* `\r\n`
* `length` bytes of content
* `\r\n`

In versions of h11 up to 0.14.0, h11 instead parsed them as:

* chunk length
* `\r\n`
* `length` bytes of content
* any two bytes

i.e. it did not validate that the trailing `\r\n` bytes were correct, and if you put 2 bytes of garbage there it would be accepted, instead of correctly rejecting the body as malformed.

By itself this is harmless. However, suppose you have a proxy or reverse-proxy that tries to analyze HTTP requests, and your proxy has a _d

summary: CVE-2025-43859 openshift-lightspeed-tech-preview/lightspeed-service-api-rhel9: h11 accepts some malformed Chunked-Encoding bodies [ols-0.3]
description:
Security Tracking Issue

Do not make this issue public.

Flaw:

---

h11 accepts some malformed Chunked-Encoding bodies  
[https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2362162](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2362162)

h11 is a Python implementation of HTTP/1.1. Prior to version 0.16.0, a leniency in h11's parsing of line terminators in chunked-coding message bodies can lead to request smuggling vulnerabilities under certain conditions. This issue has been patched in version 0.16.0. Since exploitation requires the combination of buggy h11 with a buggy (reverse) proxy, fixing either component is sufficient to mitigate this issue.

summary: Automatize Release Procedure - Bundle to Catalog
description:
Description

In the release procedure of Openshift Lightspeed, we have to wait for the bundle to be released before we update the file based catalogs. That is because the bundle image must be built and released at the moment of releasing file based catalogs. The operation of updating the FBCs are already faciliated with scripts.

To avoid manually checking the bundle release pipeline run,  updating the FBCs and creating the release objects for FBC, we need find a way in Konflux to trigger an automation (e.g. Github Action) that updates the FBC from the bundle image we just released via Konflux.

This is a major step towards automated releasing. 

This may require collaboration from Konflux team if new features are required in Konflux.

MCP Streamable HTTP
description:
## User Story

As a platform engineer, I want to track the adoption of Streamable HTTP in MCP and evaluate the deprecation of SSE so that our services stay aligned with supported and performant protocols.

**Description**

MCP recently introduced Streamable HTTP as a new transport option, in addition to stdio and SSE. Although SSE is currently unused in production, we need to assess whether it should be deprecated in favor of Streamable HTTP and ensure our system documentation and support reflect these changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Feasibility and basic testing of Streamable HTTP integration is completed.

* A decision is made on whether to deprecate SSE.

* Documentation is updated to reflect the officially supported protocols.

LLama-Index CLI version v0.12.20 contains an OS command injection vulnerability. The vulnerability arises from the improper handling of the \`--files\` argument, which is directly passed into \`os.system\`. An attacker who controls the content of this argument can inject and execute arbitrary shell commands. This vulnerability can be exploited locally if the attacker has control over the CLI arguments, and remotely if a web application calls the LLama-Index CLI with a user-controlled filename. This issue can lead to arbitrary code execution on the affec

description:
Security Tracking Issue

Do not make this issue public.

---

Langchain-community insecure XML parsing

The langchain-ai/langchain project, specifically the EverNoteLoader component, is vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) attacks due to insecure XML parsing. The affected version is 0.3.63. The vulnerability arises from the use of etree.iterparse() without disabling external entity references, which can lead to sensitive information disclosure. An attacker could exploit this by crafting a malicious XML payload that references local files, potentially exposing sensitive data such as /etc/passwd.

summary: MCP server configuration via OLSConfig CR produces invalid YAML and crashes pod
description:
### Description

When defining an MCP server in the `olsconfig` CR and toggling the **enableSSE** checkbox, the generated `olsconfig.yaml` contains invalid configuration. Specifically:

* The `sse` config entry is added correctly.
* However, the `streamable_http` section is also left in place.
* This causes a **server-side exception**: ValueError: Streamable HTTP transport selected but 'stdio' or 'sse' config should not be provided
* The pod then enters a **CrashLoopBackOff** state.

Additionally, when the **enableSSE** checkbox is _not_ checked, an empty `sse` config subpart is still created. As a result, **custom MCP servers cannot be added at all**.

---

summary: CVE-2025-47907 openshift-lightspeed-tech-preview/lightspeed-operator-bundle: Postgres Scan Race Condition [ols-1]
description:
Security Tracking Issue

Do not make this issue public.

Flaw:

---

Postgres Scan Race Condition

Cancelling a query (e.g. by cancelling the context passed to one of the query methods) during a call to the Scan method of the returned Rows can result in unexpected results if other queries are being made in parallel. This can result in a race condition that may overwrite the expected results with those of another query, causing the call to Scan to return either unexpected results from the other query or an error.

Do not make this issue public.

AIOHTTP HTTP Request/Response Smuggling

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to version 3.12.14, the Python parser is vulnerable to a request smuggling vulnerability due to not parsing trailer sections of an HTTP request. If a pure Python version of aiohttp is installed (i.e. without the usual C extensions) or AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS is enabled, then an attacker may be able to execute a request smuggling attack to bypass certain firewalls or proxy protections. Version 3.12.14 contains a patch for this issue.

The llama-index-core package, up to version 0.12.44, contains a vulnerability in the \`get_cache_dir()\` function where a predictable, hardcoded directory path \`/tmp/llama_index\` is used on Linux systems without proper security controls. The issue affects all Linux deployments where multiple users share the same system. The vulnerability is classified under CWE-379, CWE-377, and CWE-367, indicating insecure temporary file creation and potential race conditions.

summary: MCP Tool Calls Fail Due to JSON String Arguments Not Being Parsed
description:
**Summary**

MCP tool calls are failing when tool arguments contain JSON strings because the arguments are passed as string values instead of parsed JSON objects to the MCP tools.

**Environment**

* Component: OpenShift LightSpeed Service
* Files Affected:
* `ols/src/query_helpers/docs_summarizer.py` (lines 330-341)
* `ols/src/tools/tools.py` (lines 37-55)

**Bug Description**

When the LLM generates tool calls with JSON string parameters (e.g., json_patch), the tool execution fails because:

1\. LangChain preserves JSON parameters as strings in response.tool_calls  
2\. No JSON parsing occurs before passing arguments to MCP tools  
3\. MCP tools expect parsed JSON objects but receive string representations  
4\. Tool execution fails with JSON unmarshaling errors

**Steps to Reproduce**

summary: CVE-2025-62707 openshift-lightspeed-tech-preview/lightspeed-rag-tool-rhel9: pypdf affected by possible infinite loop when reading DCT inline images without EOF marker [ols-1]
description:
Security Tracking Issue

Do not make this issue public.

Flaw:

---

pypdf affected by possible infinite loop when reading DCT inline images without EOF marker

pypdf is a free and open-source pure-python PDF library. Prior to version 6.1.3, an attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to an infinite loop. This requires parsing the content stream of a page which has an inline image using the DCTDecode filter. This has been fixed in pypdf version 6.1.3.

summary: CVE-2025-58183 openshift-lightspeed/openshift-mcp-server-rhel9: Unbounded allocation when parsing GNU sparse map [ols-1]
description:
Security Tracking Issue

Do not make this issue public.

Flaw:

---

Unbounded allocation when parsing GNU sparse map

tar.Reader does not set a maximum size on the number of sparse region data blocks in GNU tar pax 1.0 sparse files. A maliciously-crafted archive containing a large number of sparse regions can cause a Reader to read an unbounded amount of data from the archive into memory. When reading from a compressed source, a small compressed input can result in large allocations.

\~\~\~

description:
Security Tracking Issue

Do not make this issue public.

Flaw:

---

containerd local privilege escalation

containerd is an open-source container runtime. Versions 0.1.0 through 1.7.28, 2.0.0-beta.0 through 2.0.6, 2.1.0-beta.0 through 2.1.4 and 2.2.0-beta.0 through 2.2.0-rc.1 have an overly broad default permission vulnerability. Directory paths \`/var/lib/containerd\`, \`/run/containerd/io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri\` and \`/run/containerd/io.containerd.sandbox.controller.v1.shim\` were all created with incorrect permissions. This issue is fixed in versions 1.7.29, 2.0.7, 2.1.5 and 2.2.0. Workarounds include updating system administrator permissions so the host can manually chmod the directories to not have group or world accessible permissions, or to run containerd in rootless mode.

summary: Unreachable MCP server causes Denial of Service
description:
Description  
OpenShift Lightspeed allows the configuration of custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers via the OLSConfig custom resource to extend the AI assistant's capabilities. A weakness exists in the handling of these external connections: if a configured MCP server is offline, non-existent, or unreachable (e.g., [http://non-exist:8888/mcp](http://non-exist:8888/mcp)), the OpenShift Lightspeed service fails to initialize the tool usage subsystem properly. This results in a comprehensive failure of tool functionality, rather than isolating and disabling only the problematic server integration.

Impact  
The AI assistant loses the ability to execute tools or perform actions on the cluster, significantly degrading its utility. Users are restricted to chat-only interactions without th

summary: Cleartext Communication with Custom MCP Servers
description:
The OpenShift Lightspeed configuration for custom MCP servers (mcpServers) is configured to use the HTTP protocol. As observed in the configuration, the url parameter specifies an insecure http:// connection. This results in the cleartext transmission of traffic between the OpenShift Lightspeed instance and the custom MCP server, violating security best practices for data-in-transit protection.

### Impact

Using unencrypted protocols exposes the communication channel to potential eavesdropping. While this does not directly compromise the OpenShift Lightspeed instance itself, it allows a suitably positioned attacker to view the context data or queries being sent to the MCP server and perform man-in-the-middle attacks.

Recommendations  
Require custom MCP servers to use TLS (HTTPS).

summary: Use of Default Service Account
description:
The lightspeed-console-plugin and lightspeed-postgres-server Deployments do not specify a serviceAccountName, causing their pods to run with the default service account. While this account currently has no special permissions, it is poor security hygiene. Any overly broad RoleBinding accidentally applied to the default service account in the future will immediately grant those permissions to these pods.

Impact  
A cluster administrator, while troubleshooting, might temporarily bind a powerful role like view or even edit to the default service account in the openshift-lightspeed namespace. If they forget to remove this binding, an attacker who later compromises the lightspeed-console-plugin pod (e.g., through a web vulnerability) would inherit these elevated permissions, allowing them to r

summary: Insecure Secret Storage: PostgreSQL Credentials in Environment Variables
description:
The lightspeed-postgres-server Deployment specifies the database password directly as an environment variable (POSTGRESQL_ADMIN_PASSWORD and POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD). Environment variables are stored in plaintext in the pod's definition and are easily accessible to any user or process with sufficient permissions to read pod specs or execute commands within the container. This practice is explicitly discouraged as it increases the risk of credential leakage through logs, crash dumps, or simple introspection.

Impact  
An attacker who compromises a pod in the same namespace with permissions to read pod definitions can easily retrieve the database password. Alternatively, if a vulnerability in the PostgreSQL container itself allows for shell access, the attacker could simply run the env command t

if (root === '\[\]' && options.parseArrays) {  
obj = utils.combine(\[\], leaf);  // No arrayLimit check  
}

Working

    quotaHandlersConfig:

Flaw:

---

Python-Multipart has Arbitrary File Write via Non-Default Configuration

Python-Multipart is a streaming multipart parser for Python. Prior to version 0.0.22, a Path Traversal vulnerability exists when using non-default configuration options \`UPLOAD_DIR\` and \`UPLOAD_KEEP_FILENAME=True\`. An attacker can write uploaded files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem by crafting a malicious filename. Users should upgrade to version 0.0.22 to receive a patch or, as a workaround, avoid using \`UPLOAD_KEEP_FILENAME=True\` in project configurations.

summary: CVE-2025-61726 openshift-lightspeed-tech-preview/lightspeed-operator-bundle: Memory exhaustion in query parameter parsing in net/url [ols-1]
description:
Security Tracking Issue

Do not make this issue public.

Flaw:

---

Memory exhaustion in query parameter parsing in net/url

The net/url package does not set a limit on the number of query parameters in a query. While the maximum size of query parameters in URLs is generally limited by the maximum request header size, the net/http.Request.ParseForm method can parse large URL-encoded forms. Parsing a large form containing many unique query parameters can cause excessive memory consumption.

A critical vulnerability exists in the NLTK downloader component of nltk/nltk, affecting all versions. This allows attackers to craft malicious zip packages that, when downloaded and extracted by NLTK, can execute arbitrary code. summary: CVE-2026-27896 openshift-lightspeed/openshift-mcp-server-rhel9: improper handling of case sensitivity [ols-1]
description:
Security Tracking Issue

Do not make this issue public.

Flaw:

---

improper handling of case sensitivity

The Go MCP SDK used Go's standard encoding/json.Unmarshal for JSON-RPC and MCP protocol message parsing in versions prior to 1.3.1. Go's standard library performs case-insensitive matching of JSON keys to struct field tags — a field tagged json:"method" would also match "Method", "METHOD", etc. This violated the JSON-RPC 2.0 specification, which defines exact field names. A malicious MCP peer may have been able to send protocol messages with non-standard field casing that the SDK would silently accept. This had the potential for bypassing intermediary inspection and coss-implementation inconsistency. Go's standard JSON unmarshaling was replaced with a case-sensitive decoder in commit

summary: Breaking CRD schema change in patch release 1.0.10 blocks upgrades from 1.0.9 for users with MCP servers
description:
Description:  
The mcpServers CRD schema was restructured between 1.0.9 and 1.0.10 (patch release)

url moved from streamableHTTP.url to a required top-level field; sseReadTimeout, enableSSE were removed

OLM validates existing CRs against the new CRD schema before upgrading, causing all upgrades to fail with RequirementsNotMet for users who have MCP servers configured

The error surfaces as misleading "ServiceAccount does not exist" on the CSV

Severity: Blocker for any 1.0.9 user with MCP servers

Fix needed: Either revert the breaking change, add backwards compatibility for the old   
schema, or provide an automated migration (conversion webhook)

SemVer violation: Breaking API changes must not ship in patch releases

summary: Remove redundant __eq__ from config models
description: Config model classes in `config.py` define 10 hand-rolled `__eq__` methods that manually compare fields one by one. Pydantic's `BaseModel` already provides identical behavior automatically. Four of these methods accidentally omit recently-added fields (`user_data_collection`, `extra_ca`, `uvicorn_port_number`, `dev_config`, etc.), meaning equality checks silently ignore those fields. The manual implementations also account for two of the highest-complexity functions in the codebase (`OLSConfig.__eq__` at CC=20, `ProviderConfig.__eq__` at CC=13). Removing all 10 eliminates \~120 lines, fixes the silent field omissions, and drops the file's complexity score significantly.

summary: Refactor tool output truncation into two-layer defense with budget enforcement
description:
**Description:**  
The current tool output truncation has two problems:

1. Individual tool outputs are tokenized even when they are very large (multi-MB), which is CPU-expensive.
2. Per-tool truncation doesn't guarantee the _combined_ tool outputs fit within the LLM context window — multiple tools can collectively overflow the budget even when each one individually fits.

Refactors tool output truncation into a two-layer defense:

**Layer 1 — Character-level pre-truncation** (`_extract_text_from_tool_output`)

* Applies a cheap character-level size guard (`max_tokens * 4 chars`) before any tokenization occurs.
* Strings are cut at the last newline boundary; list-format outputs drop trailing blocks.
* Prevents tokenizing arbitrarily large tool responses (neither LangChain nor MCP SDK provi

The `store_feedback` endpoint writes the file synchronously and returns 200 only after the write completes. However, the test reads the file via a separate `oc rsh` session, which opens a new network connection to the pod. Occasional latency in the `oc rsh` roundtrip or filesystem visibility (overlayfs / PVC) causes the `ls` to not see the file yet.

This is a timing issue, not a logic bug — the test passes on retry.

summary: Make max tool output configurable
description:
Currently the tool output truncation is driven by these constants:

```python
# Tool output token limits
# Maximum tokens for a single tool output before truncation
DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS_PER_TOOL_OUTPUT = 8000
# Total tokens reserved for all tool outputs (only used when MCP servers configured)
DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS_FOR_TOOLS = 32000
```

It’s possible that these values won’t be sufficient in scenarios where there are a large number of logs or metrics. OLS might not be able to troubleshoot if it doesn’t see all the logs.

I’m not sure that making them configurable is the only option. Perhaps this is an issue that will be addressed indirectly by offloading and context management tools.

OLS is a domain-specific agent for OpenShift/Kubernetes. To enable its use in multi-agent environments (e.g., orchestrated by ADK, or any A2A-compatible framework), OLS should expose an A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol endpoint alongside its existing REST API.

This allows an orchestrator to discover OLS as a specialized OpenShift agent, route relevant queries to it, and compose it with other agents (monitoring, CI/CD, security, etc.) without OLS-specific integration code.

**Scope**:

1. **A2A endpoint**: New endpoint implementing the A2A protocol specification (agent card, task lifecycle, streaming via SSE)
2. **Agent card**: OLS advertises its capabilities -- what it can answer, what tools it has access to, supported modes (streaming/non-streaming)
3. **Capability exposure**: Configurable

summary: Introduce TokenBudgetTracker for unified per-request token accounting
description:
**The problem**

The previous approach relied on a single available_tokens integer threaded through method calls, with no breakdown of what consumed the budget. Tool-calling rounds charged tokens via a mutable ToolTokenUsage dataclass passed between methods. AI messages emitted between rounds were not tracked at all. This made it impossible to diagnose context window exhaustion or reason about remaining budget.

**Solution**

Replace the ad-hoc token budget management scattered across DocsSummarizer with a centralized TokenBudgetTracker that tracks every token allocation by category (prompt, history, RAG, skill, tool definitions, AI rounds, tool results). **Description:**

The `consumers` block in `lightspeedopenshift` `product.yaml` was defined at the root YAML level instead of nested under the `marts` presentation schema. [UI] Re-selecting an attachment overwrites user edits
description:
When a user edits an attachment (e.g., modifies the YAML in the preview modal and saves), then selects the same resource again from the attach menu, the fresh content replaces the edited attachment, silently discarding the user's changes.

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Attach a resource (e.g., Full YAML file)
2. Click the attachment label to open the preview modal
3. Click Edit, make changes, and click Save
4. Open the attach menu and select the same resource again
5. Click the attachment label — the user's edits are gone

**Expected:** The user's edits are preserved. The "Revert to original" option updates to reflect the latest fetched content.

**Actual:** The attachment is replaced with fresh content and the edits are lost.

Make the rag-tool component pass EC checks so it can be released
description:
The rag-tool can not be released with the current EC rules for the OLS in Konflux, it trips over the following:

```
For each of the packages fetched by Hermeto which define externalReferences, verify they are allowed based on the allowed_package_sources rule data key. By default, allowed_package_sources is empty, which means no components with such references are allowed. To exclude this rule add "sbom_spdx.allowed_package_sources:pkg:pypi/torch?checksum=sha256:e42ab849b64444059f5eda352d61c9c3a078f30797e48e2972857182c9a00cf8&download_url=https://packages.redhat.com/api/pulp-content/public-rhai/rhoai/3.3/cpu-ubi9/torch-2.9.1-4-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl" to the `exclude` section of the policy configuration.
```

AC:  
The rag-tool component passes EC checks and can be released.

summary: Small Content Updates
description:
General comments from peer review pertaining to the following assembly or the modules within it:  
configure/ols-configuring-openshift-lightspeed.adoc

* There are a few references to the "plus button". See SSG about icon descriptions / "plus sign" and consider whether click **Add** might be more appropriate.
* There are a few references of /path/to/ in example commands. See repo guidelines and SSG for showing those as user-replaceables, e.g. <path>/config-cr.yaml or <path_to_file>/config-cr.yaml.
* The 2 "Granting access to..." procedures are currently single-step procedures, so they should be using a \* (unordered bullet) instead of a . (numbered list) per SSG. However, I think alternatively there is likely a way you could split up the single-step into multi-steps, though maybe a little

summary: [UI] Add attach logs option for CronJob
description:
## Story

We currently support attaching logs for various k8s resource types, but not for CronJobs.

The UX should be the same as for Deployment, Job, etc., but for CronJobs some more work is required to find the list of relevant pods.

See similar logic in the Console code base here: [https://github.com/openshift/console/blob/master/frontend/public/components/cron-job.tsx](https://github.com/openshift/console/blob/master/frontend/public/components/cron-job.tsx))

## Acceptance Criteria

* Attach logs option is available on the CronJob details page.
